findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Waste and Recycling Budget and Costs - July 2026
findings.headline: First full year (2025/26) balanced budget rests on £2m Extended Producer Responsibility grant described as uncertain
findings.detail: Service reported balanced budget at 2025/26 year-end: actual costs £8.678m against budget £8.7m. This required £2m pEPR grant funding (out of £2.4m received; £0.4m set aside in reserve). Without grant, costs would have been £10.7m. Council acknowledges future pEPR funding levels are uncertain and whether it will impact Welsh Government's future funding to councils.
findings.matters: Reported balanced budget masks underlying costs of £10.7m that would be unaffordable without continued uncertain grant funding
findings.figures: Reported cost £8.678m; pEPR grant £2m used (£2.4m total received); underlying cost without pEPR £10.7m; budget £8.7m
findings.quote: What is uncertain is how much that funding will be, and whether it impacts in anyway on WG's future funding to Council's in Wales.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Waste and Recycling Budget and Costs - July 2026
findings.headline: Service overspent by £2m–£3m in transition year (2024/25) on budget the council knew was underfunded
findings.detail: Service overspent by £800k in 2023/24 against £7.2m budget. Council chose not to address this shortfall when setting 2024/25 budget at £7.2m. In transition year, actual costs were £10.4m (£9.2m net of £1.2m one-off income), producing reported overspend of £2m (£3.2m excluding one-off income). Overspend driven by agency staff, overtime, and temporary vehicle hire during operational transition.
findings.matters: A £2–3m overspend following a consciously underfunded budget indicates control issues and service delivery risk
findings.figures: 2024/25 budget £7.2m; actual costs £10.4m; reported overspend £2m (£3.2m before one-off income); prior underfunding £800k
findings.quote: Note that we knew that the waste service was under-funded by £800k but we chose not to address that in the budget for 2024/25 for the reasons explained above.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Waste and Recycling Budget and Costs - July 2026
findings.headline: Capital project overran approved budget by £1.5m, funded partly by £6.4m prudential borrowing
findings.detail: Initial estimate from 2018 was £12.4m. Final business case budget was £21.6m, with additional £1.3m approved October 2024 for total approved budget of £22.9m. Actual outturn was £24.4m. Funded through £6.4m of service-funded prudential borrowing, £13m Welsh Government grants, £3m general capital funding, and £1.9m reserves.
findings.matters: A £1.5m capital overrun (6.5%) signals project delivery risk, and the council must service £6.4m of borrowed capital
findings.figures: Approved budget £22.9m; Actual £24.4m; Prudential Borrowing £6.4m; WG Grants £13m
findings.quote: The project had been in the planning since 2018 with an initial capital cost of £12.4m. As is often the case with significant and complex capital projects that span over several years, the project had evolved over time and the capital costs changed as a result.

findings.paper_title: App 2 - Denbighshire CC Final Audit of Accounts Report 2022-23
findings.headline: Related party disclosure incomplete; elected member failed to declare directorships in organisations with council contracts
findings.detail: Testing identified one elected member who had failed to declare directorships in two organisations; review found transactions between the council and both organisations that should have been disclosed in the related party notes. Another member's declaration was not available at time of audit. This indicates weak governance controls over member declarations and potential transparency failures.
findings.matters: Incomplete related party disclosures represent a governance and transparency failure that concerns lenders. They obscure potential conflicts of interest and may indicate weaker oversight of member conduct and council spending.
findings.figures: One elected member's undeclared directorships in two organisations; transactions identified but not originally disclosed
findings.quote: One elected member had failed to declare their directorship in two organisations. Review identified transactions between the Council and both organisations, which should have been included in the disclosures in Note 32.

findings.paper_title: App 2 - Denbighshire CC Final Audit of Accounts Report 2022-23
findings.headline: Systematic failures in transaction population reconciliation requiring significant rework
findings.detail: The audit team encountered significant difficulties reconciling populations for employee benefit expenses, fees and charges income, and other service expenditure. The financial ledger structure did not allow a single auditable population to be formed, requiring many reports to be generated and manually combined, consuming considerable time from both audit and finance staff.
findings.matters: This indicates fundamental weaknesses in the council's financial ledger and reporting controls, making it difficult to verify the accuracy and completeness of financial statements. It suggests the finance function lacks robust systems for transaction classification and reporting.
findings.figures: Not quantified, but described as requiring 'considerable amount of time' from both audit and finance teams
findings.quote: During the audit, the audit team encountered significant difficulties in reconciling populations for several classes of transaction including employee benefit expenses, fees, charges and other service income and other service expenditure. The structure of the financial ledger did not allow for a single population to be formed for the transaction lines within Note 5 to the financial statements. Many reports had to be generated from the ledger and combined, to create one transaction level population that was auditable.
